title: Transform of 3D nodes is broken when using threaded processing.
body: ### Tested versions Reproducible in 4.6 stable. ### System information Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS 22.04 on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-13900HX (32 threads) - 31.03 GiB memory ### Issue description Under certain configurations (having multiple threaded node subtrees, or setting `process_thread_group` at runtime), visual transformation of certain Node3Ds are erratic when threaded processing is enabled for them. See steps to reproduce for detailed description of an example case. ### Steps to reproduce In the MRP, we have a scene with this structure: where `direct_child` is the white sphere, `threaded_node_root` is the white torus. The script attached to `parent_main` is: ```gdscript extends Node3D var total_time := 0.0 func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void: total_time += delta position.x = sin(total_time) $threaded_node_root.set_deferred_thread_group(&'total_time', total_time) ``` The script attached to `threaded_node_root` is: ```gdscript extends Node3D var total_time := 0.0 func _ready() -> void: process_thread_messages = Node.FLAG_PROCESS_THREAD_MESSAGES_ALL process_thread_group = Node.PROCESS_THREAD_GROUP_SUB_THREAD func _physics_process(_delta: float) -> void: $direct_child.position.y = cos(total_time) $intermediate/indirect_child.position.y = cos(total_time) ``` These script should move the nodes along a circular trajectory. That is, the expected behavior is as follows: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e49ff37a-1805-4806-95fc-44c3c8ebeb6a However, the actual behavior is different. ### Case 1: When `threaded_node_root.process_thread_group` is set to sub thread *in the editor*, the result is: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7e537ab7-34e6-4d6b-97a7-8643235e5d4a As you can see, the `MeshInstance3D` nodes randomly malfunctions (this clearly indicates some race conditions). ### Case 2: When `threaded_node_root.process_thread_group` is defaulted to inherit (manually reset it in the MRP), and is set to sub thread in the code via `_ready`, the result is: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1d46cff8-cda1-4ef2-be84-dd3d6fc2b323 This time the meshes do not get stuck, but transform of them are not properly updated. X-axis movement is driven by `parent_in_main`, which runs in the main thread. Y-axis movement is driven by `threaded_node_root`. Only X-axis movement is working in this case, and the debug panel is filled with this message: ``` E 0:00:00:765 threaded_scene.gd:10 @ _physics_process(): /root/Node3D/parent_in_main/threaded_node_root/direct_child: The caller thread can't call the function `set_position()` on this node. Use `call_deferred()` or `call_deferred_thread_group()` instead. Condition "!is_accessible_from_caller_thread()" is true. scene/3d/node_3d.cpp:708 @ set_position() threaded_scene.gd:10 @ _physics_process() ``` which indicates that thread group of children of `threaded_node_root` is not properly setup when `threaded_node_root.process_thread_group` is set through code at runtime. (The `threaded_node_root` is indeed running in another thread, as `Thread.is_main_thread()` returns `false` in its `_physics_process()`) I think I have figured out what's wrong in the code and fixed it, and I am submitting [PR#116000](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/116000) now. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [threaded_fix_demo.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25144218/threaded_fix_demo.zip)
